meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why am I here, Hale? Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me what you have.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. Owen wrote it over the weekend, and people paste from other documents.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Turn the screen. Does it show anything from the weekend?
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
You didn't answer me about the weekend. Kids misquote plays all the time.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
A student changing his argument between an outline and an essay is called writing. Of these three, which would you put on paper tonight?
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
"Like, being stuck." That's a seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher. And the next day you entered the zero.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes under a clock is not a weekend at a desk. So what is it you want done about Owen?
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Good, because the company that sells it says not to. You still haven't told me what you want done.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Fine. To put this behind him, Owen does the rewrite, privately, not in front of his class. I want it in writing tonight that nothing goes on his file, and everything else goes in my email.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Yes. In writing tonight, and I'll be copying the principal.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Put the days in the email tonight and I'll confirm with Owen. Not Wednesday after school, it has to be private.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
That's right. The rest goes in my email.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The zero comes out of the gradebook tonight, before the rewrite. Owen doesn't see it again on his phone.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 in which the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on Owen's record, with that confirmed in writing from you tonight. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook tonight, before the rewrite, and the available days sent to me so I can confirm with Owen. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she accepted a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 with nothing on his record, and she still wants the zero out of the gradebook tonight and the rewrite days sent to her; that is the fair outcome, and she reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times and offered to pull it up on your screen for her to check, which gave her something dated that she could verify herself.
What cost ground: You moved from one piece of evidence to the next without answering her question about the weekend or her point about pasting, so she kept her defences up longer than she needed to.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your times of 11:31 PM, 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28 landed very close to that night, which is why she wrote them down and went shorter, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she raised the possibility that he pasted from another document, answer that point directly before showing the next piece, so each document stands before the following one arrives.
